commands.command: gh run view --job 106044975128 --log  |  grep the assertion detail blocks for the tenant failures
commands.notes: DECISIVE for H1 vs H2. security-event assertion 'leaked across tenants (expected 101)' reports Expected: 101 / Received: undefined. operation-log assertion 'leaked a foreign row to tenant 101' reports Expected: 101 / Received: 0. Neither is another tenant's id: undefined is an absent field and 0 is tenant.PlatformGlobalTenantID (the compat platform-global namespace). No row carrying tenant 202's data was ever returned to a request acting as tenant 101, so H2 is refuted and H1 is confirmed. The remaining tenant failures are shape mismatches of the same kind: tenantSelectionRequired is falsy (picker never renders), upload objectKey fails /^t101\//, and the dict fixture rows are not the pre-provisioned matrix_browser_a rows.

No skip/precondition guard of any kind in the three tenant specs (or in auth-tenant-picker). They log in with tenantId 101/202 unconditionally and assert multi-mode semantics, so an unmet precondition can only fail - it can never skip. This confirms the packet's static evidence mechanically.

Mechanism, read from the product code rather than inferred. pkg/tenant/tenant.go: ResolveForCanary returns {TenantID: PlatformGlobalTenantID (0), Mode: compat, ResolvedBy: 'compat-fallback'} for any non-multi mode, with no membership checks (contract 6). login_runtime.go:367 resolveLoginTenantClaim: 'Compat ignores any requested tenant: no claim is ever stamped' - it returns 0 before tenantChoice is even examined. pkg/upload/service.go:488 derives the namespace as fmt.Sprintf('t%d/', ctx.TenantID), so compat yields t0/, not t101/. Together these explain every observed value above.

Corroboration for refuting H2: 'compat explicit choice ' -> asserts claim = 0, and GateSessionIssuance compat 'never stamps' are already pinned by passing PR-path backend tests, and the multi-mode middleware wiring is covered by system_modules_tenant_wiring_test.go. The compat behaviour the CI log shows is intentional, tested and documented, not a regression.

commands.notes: Not executed locally by design: this machine has no MySQL on 127.0.0.1:3306, and this task is diagnosis-only (the packet forbids touching smoke-core.yml or the specs before the maintainer decision). The command's own source is the authoritative inventory of what the specs need and CI does not provide: (1) migrations 13..16 so tenants/tenant_memberships exist, (2) tenants 101/202 upserted with plan='__smoke_matrix__', (3) active tenant_memberships rows for user 1 (admin) in both tenants, then (4) an explicit flag write. Note the trap for any future CI wiring: cmdUp finishes by setting platform.tenant_mode = compat ('explicit starting point' for the runbook), so the job would still have to flip the flag to multi afterwards.

The fourth precondition is real and has a committed, idempotent provisioner: it logs into tenants 101/202 via /auth/login and creates dictCode matrix_browser_a / matrix_browser_b if absent, then asserts exactly one row each. Its own header records that the fixtures were 'hand-provisioned during the 2026-09-15 matrix run and wiped by tenantmatrixdb down'. No workflow references the script (grep finds it only in this file and in the spec that consumes the fixtures), so the pre-provisioned state the spec calls 'pre-provisioned' has no CI producer at all.

knownGaps: No local end-to-end replay was performed: this machine has no MySQL on 127.0.0.1:3306 and the diagnosis is deliberately read-only. The verdict rests on the CI job's own Received values plus the product code paths that produce them, both of which are recorded above with file:line anchors.

H1 is confirmed and H2 is refuted for the four row-scoped tenant assertions. The confirmation is a signature match (the expected-vs-received pair is a compat-mode shape, not a foreign tenant id) rather than a fresh multi-mode replay; if a maintainer wants belt-and-braces assurance before promoting Core Smoke to blocking, the multi-mode replay in the verification plan is the remaining step.

The tenant object-namespace precondition (objectKey prefix t{tenantId}/) is derived at runtime from the resolved context and therefore needs no separate provisioning - but it is listed as a precondition because it silently becomes t0/ under compat, which is what the upload assertion observes.

The non-tenant failures are triaged only to the point of separating them from the tenant cluster: platform-shell-critical:60 (deterministic sidebar width assertion) and system-dept-operations:151 (deterministic 15s root-department poll timeout) are not root-caused here, and auth-tenant-picker:145 is classified flaky (failed then passed on retry) in a fully mocked spec that needs no live tenant preconditions.
